memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And if it is true and it has been proved that this detestable thing has been done in Israel, take the man or woman who has done this evil deed to your city gate and stone that person to death. On the testimony of two or three witnesses a person is to be put to death, but no one is to be put to death on the testimony of only one witness. - Deut 17:4b-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we should not soften it. Under Israel's covenant law, the penalty for leading the nation into idolatry was death. To modern ears this sounds severe, but we must remember what was at stake, the survival of a people God had set apart to bring blessing and, eventually, the Messiah to the whole world. Idolatry threatened to corrupt them entirely.

Yet even here, God builds in strong protection for the accused. No one could be condemned on the word of a single witness. It required two or three witnesses, and the charge had to be proven true. God guarded against false accusation and personal vendettas. Justice had to be careful and certain, never careless.

We live in a different covenant moment. Jesus came not to condemn sinners but to save them, and He Himself bore the penalty our sin deserved (John 3:17). When a woman caught in sin was dragged before Him, He did not stone her; He offered mercy and called her to leave her sin (John 8:11). The seriousness of sin has not lessened, but at the cross Christ absorbed the judgment we could not survive. And the principle of requiring reliable witnesses still shapes godly justice today. How does the cross change the way you view your own sin, and God's mercy?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does the seriousness of sin still weigh on your heart?
2. How does Christ bearing our judgment move you to worship?
3. Where do you need to receive or extend mercy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Jesus bore the judgment my sin deserved. Help me hate sin rightly and rest fully in Your mercy. Amen.
